request.message:
Okay, we're going to build a complex workflow, parallel paths.

GrassValley is going to output SRT which would go into Uplynk. Through Uplynk we would then go into a live event.

Then we have another partner who is going to send us an HLS feed. That'll go through Uplynk into a live channel. The live channel will output OTT and will publish to YouTube.

reply: Set up two independent paths through Uplynk. Grass Valley's SRT feed goes through ingest and transcode into the live event, and the partner's HLS feed goes through ingest and transmux into the channel, which then feeds both your own OTT app and YouTube. I split Uplynk into its individual steps since a live event or channel can't be fed straight from the all-in-one Uplynk box — worth confirming that's fine.
summary: Built two parallel paths: a Grass Valley SRT feed transcoded into a live event, and a partner HLS feed transmuxed into a linear channel publishing to OTT and YouTube.

request.message:
On the top track, we're going to do redundancy there. So we're going to get another SRT signal that's going to follow the exact same path as the existing one. It's going to go to its own event, ingest, event transcode, and then it's going to feed into the same live event.
This is our failover redundancy part.

reply: Added the backup SRT path — new Grass Valley MCR, ingest, and transcode all feeding into the same live event for failover. Also gave the live event its own OTT output as noted; the channel already has a separate OTT output since each source needs its own per the rules.
summary: Added a redundant SRT path (Grass Valley MCR → ingest → transcode) feeding the same live event for failover, and gave the event its own OTT output.
